What is Derivative?
A derivative is a financial contract whose value is derived from the value of an underlying asset.
The underlying asset can be:
Shares / stocks
Bonds
Currencies
Commodities
Interest rates
Market indices
Simple example:
If a derivative is based on the price of Reliance shares, the derivative's value will change according to the price of Reliance shares.

4 Main Types of Derivatives
Type :-
1. Forward
OTC (Over-the-Counter) contract.
Customized between two parties.
Settlement takes place in the future.
Higher counterparty risk.
Example: An importer agrees today to buy $100,000 after 3 months at ₹85/USD.

2. Futures
Traded on a stock exchange.
Standardized contract.
Requires margin.
Lower counterparty risk because of clearing houses.
Example: Buying Nifty Futures expecting the Nifty index to rise.

3. Options
An option gives the buyer a right but not an obligation.
Two types:
Call Option: Right to buy
Put Option: Right to sell
The buyer pays a premium for this right.

4. Swaps
A swap is an agreement between two parties to exchange cash flows.
Common types:
Interest Rate Swap
Currency Swap
Commodity Swap
Credit Default Swap (CDS)
Example: A company with a floating-rate loan may enter into an interest rate swap to exchange floating interest payments for fixed payments.
